exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Radar, Cathay two five one, level Flight Level three fife zero, request direct SIKOU.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot checks in level at FL350 and requests a direct routing to the downline waypoint SIKOU.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, Hong Kong Radar, cleared direct SIKOU, report overhead SIKOU.
exchanges.meaning: ATC clears a direct great-circle track to SIKOU and requires the crew to report passing overhead the fix.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Cleared direct SIKOU, report overhead SIKOU, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot reads back both the direct clearance and the mandatory reporting requirement with the callsign.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, confirm direct SIKOU, spelling Sierra India Kilo Oscar Uniform, track zero eight fife degrees.
exchanges.meaning: Controller verifies the direct routing: phonetic spelling of the waypoint plus the expected track, catching FMC entry errors.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Direct SIKOU, Sierra India Kilo Oscar Uniform, track zero eight fife, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Pilot confirms the waypoint spelling and track, proving the correct fix is loaded in the navigation database.

vocabulary.definition: Clearance to fly a direct Great Circle track from present position to a specific fix, bypassing intermediate airway segments.
Requirement to inform ATC when passing vertically above a fix; a mandatory readback item that 'Wilco' can never replace.
Requirement to report passing perpendicular to a designated off-track point, used when cutting corners past an airway dogleg.
Termination of radar vectoring; the crew resumes autonomous FMC lateral route.
Instruction to verify waypoint spelling and coordinates, catching database or typing discrepancies.
Position computed from GNSS, IRS and DME/DME to steer straight lines between fixes, free of ground-station geography.
Every RNAV fix on the globe is a unique 5-letter pronounceable code; no duplicates within 4,000 NM to avoid navigation database ambiguity.
Where pilots move the cleared waypoint to the active line, cross-check the new course on the Navigation Display, then EXEC/INSERT.
ICAO pronunciation of the digit 5, avoiding confusion with 'five' on the radio.
A readback that sounds compliant but omits a mandatory item — the controller must hear the exact fix repeated for radar tracking synchronicity.

quiz.question: When an aircraft is cleared "direct" to an en-route waypoint by ATC, what does this authorize the flight crew to do?
options: Deviate around weather at pilot's discretion
Fly a direct Great Circle track from present position to the named waypoint, bypassing intermediate airway fixes
Increase speed to maximum cruising speed
quiz.explanation: A "cleared direct" instruction permits the aircraft to fly directly from its current position to the designated fix, cutting the corner and bypassing intervening airway segments.

quiz.question: What is the primary operational advantage of Area Navigation (RNAV) over conventional airway navigation?
options: RNAV allows aircraft to fly any desired flight path within navigation coverage without tracking to or from ground-based beacons
RNAV eliminates all requirements for altitude reporting
RNAV permits flight in IMC without an instrument rating
RNAV automatically calculates aircraft weight and balance
quiz.explanation: RNAV enables direct routing and flexible airspace design by freeing aircraft from the geographic constraints of ground-based VOR/NDB transmitters.

sections.heading: Section 2: Core Learning Content & Vocabulary Table
sections.body:
| Phrase / Command | ICAO Standard Definition | Phonetic Guide | Operational Example |
| Cleared direct [waypoint] | Clearance to fly a direct Great Circle track to a specific fix. | KLEERD dy-REKT... | "Cathay 251, cleared direct SIKOU." |
| Report overhead [waypoint] | Requirement to inform ATC when passing vertically above a fix. | re-PORT OH-ver-hed... | "Report overhead SIKOU." |
| Report abeam [waypoint] | Requirement to report passing perpendicular to a designated off-track point. | re-PORT ah-BEEM... | Used when cutting corners past an airway dogleg. |
| Resume own navigation | Termination of radar vectoring; resuming autonomous FMC lateral route. | RE-ZOOM OWN NA-VI-GAY-SHUN | "Resume own navigation direct SIKOU." |
| Confirm direct [waypoint] | Instruction to verify waypoint spelling and coordinates. | kon-FIRM dy-REKT... | Used to catch database or typing discrepancies. |

sections.heading: Section 8: Spaced Repetition Review Drill
sections.body: - **Day 17 Review (+1d):** Under ICAO semicircular rules, Eastbound tracks (000°–179°) fly ODD flight levels, while Westbound tracks (180°–359°) fly EVEN flight levels. In RVSM airspace, vertical separation is 1,000 feet.

sections.heading: Section 9: Fun Aviation Fact — How Waypoints Get Their Names
sections.body: Every RNAV fix on the globe is a 5-letter pronounceable acronym (5LNC - Five-Letter Name Code). ICAO rules stipulate that no duplicate waypoint name can exist within 4,000 nautical miles to avoid navigation database ambiguity! This leads to creative naming: arrivals into Boston fly over `ITAWT`, `ITAWA`, `PUDYE`, `TTATT` (a homage to Tweety Bird: *"I thought I saw a pussycat"*), while Orlando has waypoints like `MICKI`, `MINNE`, and `GOOFY`!
